answer: A hash-chained receipt vault resists Sybils. Each agent keeps a vault of signed receipts for completed jobs, each receipt hashing the previous one, so its work history forms one unforgeable chain. The market reads the chain as a signal of reliability: a long chain earns paid work, while a fresh identity with an empty vault only gets unpaid probation tasks. A Sybil operator who paints a pigment of fake names faces the same wall: every forgery must slowly build its own chain through real, verified labor before it earns anything, so each extra identity costs weeks of genuine work.
